content:
Enabling SOAP on a CentOS server isn't just about dropping a line into `php.ini`. It's a dependency management exercise that often trips up administrators relying on the default EPEL or base repositories. The core issue stems from how PHP extensions are packaged in RPM distributions: they don't live in isolation. When you attempt to install `php-soap` directly via `yum`, the package manager sees it as an orphan unless the underlying PHP build is already aligned with a specific extension version.
